The “for guests” dinner set **gathering dust** in the cabinet for decades.
Appliance boxes and jars in the garage “because they’ll **come in handy someday**.”
**Expired meds** in the cabinet and five-year-old spices.
“When I lose weight” clothes and “just in case” stuff — they keep you **waiting for the worst**.

t: 8 UNWRITTEN RULES THAT MAKE LIFE EASIER RIGHT AWAY
l: Don’t lend money to relatives. As the saying goes, **money and family don’t mix**.
Don’t shake hands sitting down. A small thing people **judge you by**.
Don’t hand things over or say hello **across a doorway**. Step inside — it’s simply more respectful.
Don’t share too much about yourself. Not everyone **wishes you well**.
As a guest, don’t criticize the food. If they **welcome you to the table** — sit down and eat.
Don’t take **the last piece** from a shared plate unless you brought it.
Keep quiet about your income and plans. Speech is **silver**, silence is **golden**.
**Look people in the eye** when you listen.

t: 5 THINGS NEVER TO DO IF YOU DON’T WANT TO DESTROY YOURSELF FROM WITHIN
l: Never talk about a dream before it comes true. Don’t **count your chickens** before they hatch.
Never sink into others’ problems as if they were yours. It’s easy to fix others’ troubles — **hard to fix your own**.
Never get so attached that without that person **there’s nothing left of you**.
Never borrow and never lend. Debts **ruin both families and friendships**.
Never brag about the good you’ve done. Say it out loud — and it’s **no longer yours**.

t: 16 HEALTH PROBLEMS FUELED BY EVERYDAY HABITS
l: HEART — **lack of movement**
OSTEOPOROSIS — **lack of sun and movement**
TYPE 2 DIABETES — **sweets and extra weight**
HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE — **too much salt**
MIGRAINE — **skipped meals**
GASTRITIS — **alcohol and painkillers on an empty stomach**
HEARTBURN — lying down **right after eating**
ANEMIA — tea and coffee with **low iron**
CONSTIPATION — **too little water and fiber**
ASTHMA ATTACKS — **indoor dust**
LIVER — **alcohol and fried food**
VITAMIN D DEFICIENCY — **rarely going outside**
KIDNEY STONES — **not enough water**
DEMENTIA RISK — **loneliness and lack of movement**
INSOMNIA — **screens before bed**
ANXIETY — can get worse with **constant social media**

t: 10 HABITS THAT DRAG YOU DOWN
l: Putting up with what you don’t like because “**it’ll work out somehow**.”
Hanging out with people who **crush your self-esteem**.
Living in constant fear of “**what will people say**.”
**Holding back your feelings** and opinions.
Trying to **please everyone**.
**Always rushing**.
**Fearing mistakes**.
**Comparing yourself** to others.
Setting yourself up **for failure** in advance.
Thinking about everyone **except yourself**.

t: 7 HABITS OF PEOPLE WHO NEVER RUN OUT OF MONEY
l: They track **every expense** — in an app or a notebook by the fridge.
They save part of their income first, not “whatever’s left.” Saving for a **rainy day** isn’t pessimism — it’s a habit.
They keep their **money in order**. They say poverty follows those who stuff bills anywhere in a rush.
They never carry an **empty wallet** — at least one coin should always be there.
They don’t borrow **for status**: not for a wedding “like everyone else’s,” not for a phone to keep up with the Joneses.
They don’t lend **on impulse** or without agreeing on a deadline. Either help for good or say no right away.
They stick with people who also **count their money** and don’t laugh at it.

t: 5 MONEY RULES AFTER 50 NOBODY LIKES TO TALK ABOUT
l: Don’t count on your pension to support you. A pension isn’t a life plan — **it’s a safety net**.
Be ready to work after 60 — but **by your own choice**. Better your own business than any job out of desperation.
Keep a cushion of at least three months. Not for vacations — **for medicine, bills, and teeth**.
Watch out for scammers. Never read out card details or one-time codes by phone: people over 50 are **targeted most often**.
Pay off the loans with the **highest interest** first. Debt eats your peace faster than any price hike.

t: PERSISTENCE BEATS EVERYTHING. PERIOD.
l: Nothing in the world can take the place of plain **persistence**.
Talent? No — so many talented people **never achieve anything**.
Genius? No — the “unrecognized genius” is a **worn-out cliché**.
Education? No — the world is full of **educated fools**.
Only persistence and determination can **move mountains**.

t: HOW ONE THOUGHT BECOMES YOUR DESTINY
l: Watch your thoughts — they become **words**.
Watch your words — they become **actions**.
Watch your actions — they become **behavior**.
Watch your behavior — it becomes **habit**.
Watch your habits — they become **character**.
Watch your character — it becomes your **destiny**.

t: SO HOW ARE YOU LIVING YOUR LIFE?
l: Humble — you **go unnoticed**.
Strong — people **fear you**.
Kind — people **use you**.
Honest — people **judge you**.
Successful — people **envy you**.
Different — people **don’t get you**.
So who do you really want **to be**?

t: THE DUMBEST LOGIC MOST PEOPLE LIVE BY
l: Starting a business for $1,000 — too expensive. Buying a new iPhone for $1,000 — **stylish**.
Healthy food for $100 — too much. Dinner out for $100 — **awesome**.
Spending an hour and a half a day on a new skill — too hard. Two hours on a TV show — **totally normal**.
Life is made of daily choices, and **you** are the one who has to make them.

t: DO YOU REALLY HAVE THAT MANY PROBLEMS?
l: Remember: while you’re healthy, you have countless problems. Once you get sick — **only one is left**.
That’s why your health comes **first** — before all other tasks, plans, and chores.
If you’re not healthy, everything else **loses its meaning**.
So protect and value your body — health is the **most precious thing** you have.

t: A WISE JAPANESE PROVERB ABOUT LOSS
l: Missed the bus — maybe you **avoided an accident**.
You were turned down — maybe you were saved from **the wrong path**.
Someone left your life — maybe they **made room** for someone meant to stay.
Not every loss is a punishment. Not every delay is a step back. Sometimes life is **protecting you** from what you can’t see yet.

t: SEVEN TRUTHS ABOUT LIFE
l: A salary is a **drug** they give you so you forget your dreams.
Waiting for the perfect moment, you waste your whole life. **Start now.**
You’ll lose **90% of your friends** the moment you start growing and improving your life.
You grow up when you learn not to take everything **to heart**.
You don’t need success advice — you just need **consistency** in what you do.
The hardest thing is to focus on the good; **the easiest** is to complain about the bad.
You’ll find **peace and balance** when you learn to accept people and circumstances in your favor.

t: YOUR FATHER
l: Your father is the only man who truly wanted you to become **better than him**.
There’s no other man who wishes this for you **more**.
Most people compete with you — only he wants to see **you win**.
Have you told him you’re **grateful** for that?

t: THREE TRAITS TO LOOK FOR IN A PERSON
l: Look for three traits: **intelligence**, **energy**, and **integrity**.
If the last one is missing — **don’t even bother** with the first two.

t: WHAT IS THE MEANING OF LIFE?
l: Whoever died yesterday may still have been **thinking about tomorrow**.
Whoever died this morning may still have been **planning the evening**.
It can all end in a moment. You never **know what comes next**.
The secret is that in this world **only you truly exist**. You’re here — the world exists. You’re gone — the world is gone too.

t: THE SECRET OF WEALTH
l: Think positive. Don’t program yourself for poverty. Don’t say “I can’t.” First believe you **can change your life**.
Don’t tell everyone your plans. **Talk less, do more.** While others discuss goals, you calmly walk your path.
Don’t trust everyone. Not everyone wants you to succeed. Sometimes even loved ones belittle your dreams or **envy you**.
Watch your circle. If people keep saying “it won’t work” — ask yourself **whether to listen to them at all**.
And most of all: don’t prove to anyone you’ll be rich. Work quietly, grow — and one day **your results will speak for you**.

t: 7 QUALITIES THAT MAKE YOU TRULY HUMAN
l: **Humanity** — not walking past someone else's pain.
**Decency** — keeping your word, even when it doesn't pay.
**Truth** — speaking honestly, but without cruelty.
**Gratitude** — remembering who stood by you in hard times.
**Respect** — talking the same way to the CEO and to the cleaner.
**Conscience** — sleeping peacefully because you betrayed no one.
**Kindness** — helping even when no one is watching.
